title: Enterprise security boarding pocket guide
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, field-ready pocket guide for Solutions and CS teams handling initial enterprise security reviews and questionnaires. The goal is to speed up first-touch responses, highlight reliable artifacts to attach, and provide safe, templated language for common questions about RBAC v2, audit logs, SIEM export, and our evidence automation path.

Intended audience:
- Solutions engineers responding to RFPs and security intake
- Customer security reviewers during onboarding
- Sales engineers preparing pre-demo security notes

High-level talking points (1-minute soundbites):
- RBAC v2: role-first model with attribute assertions and least-privilege defaults; separation between control plane and data plane; roles are tenant-scoped by default.
- Audit logs: immutable, append-only event stream with user, actor, request-id, model-version, and resource-context fields; retention configurable by plan and can be exported to customer SIEM via secure S3/Kinesis endpoints.
- Evidence automation: CSV/JSON bundle generator + artifact referencing so we can produce consistent questionnaire attachments quickly.
- SIEM export: supports JSON line-format and Common Event Format (CEF) adapters; encryption in transit and at rest; delivery via customer-managed ingest endpoints or our managed export connectors.

Quick artifact map (go-to attachments to include with initial response):
- RBAC: RBAC-v2-summary.pdf (diagram + role labels)
- Audit logs: audit-log-schema-2025-06.csv (column descriptions)
- SIEM export: siem-export-options-one-pager.pdf
- Automation: evidence-bundle-sample.json (example output of evidence automation job)
- Controls: SOC2-controls-matrix-redwood-summary.pdf (redacted)

Preferred short answers (copyable snippets):
- "How is access controlled?"
  "Access is governed by RBAC v2: roles map to permission sets and are applied at the tenant level. Administrative and data-plane roles are separated and changes to role assignments are logged and auditable. We enforce least privilege and offer time-bound role grants for temporary access""

- "What does your audit log include?"
  "Our audit logs capture actor identity, request and response metadata (request_id, endpoint, model_version), resource context, timestamps, and outcome codes. Logs are written to an append-only store, signed at write-time, and retained per customer retention policy."

- "Can we ingest logs into our SIEM?"
  "Yes — we provide configurable exports in JSON Lines and CEF, delivered to customer-managed S3 buckets or pushed to an HTTP ingest endpoint with mTLS. We also support streaming via Kinesis/Cloud PubSub for higher-throughput customers. All transports are encrypted and authenticated."

Common questionnaire themes and suggested attachments:
- Data residency / export: attach the private-deployments-region-matrix + export-policy-snippet.
- Privileged access: attach PAM-process-overview and time-bound-grants-example.
- Change control: attach release-engineering-tagging-policy + documented rollout A/B canary steps.
- Incident response: attach incident-runbook-exec-summary and typical SLA thresholds.

RBAC v2 quick reference (short):
- Role model: roles -> permissions -> resource-scoped assignments
- Scopes: tenant, project, model-instance
- Grant types: permanent, temporary (TTL), approval-workflow
- Admin separation: control-plane admin vs runtime operator
- Audit hooks: every role-change emits an audit event with before/after fingerprint

Audit log schema snapshot (plain English sample):
- timestamp: ISO-8601
- request_id: uuid
- actor_type: human | service
- actor_id: user@example.com or service:sa-123
- event_type: auth | role_change | inference_request | model_deploy | config_change
- resource: /tenants/{t}/models/{m}/routes/{r}
- model_version: semantic tag or sha-identifier
- latency_ms: integer
- status_code: http-like or internal code
- raw_payload_ref: s3://customer-evidence/12345 (optional)
Notes: signed digest and sequence number appended in metadata. We keep partitioned indices for quick query.

SIEM export patterns (operational notes):
- Batch export: daily JSONL files, compressed, uploaded to customer S3 with pre-signed URL rotation.
- Streaming: message-per-event over Kinesis/PS with optional batching at delivery.
- Schema mapping: we maintain a mapping table from Redwood fields -> CEF fields; customers can request custom mapping for field names.

Evidence automation flow (how we speed answers):
- Input: questionnaire (CSV/JSON) or list of control ids
- Runner: evidence-generator service matches questions -> artifacts -> templates
- Output: zip of artifacts + a short-response file with templated language and references to live artifacts (Confluence/Storage links)
- Manual: reviewer can mark sensitive attachments as redacted before sending
- Current gaps: automated redaction of IPs in logs; live sync for private-deployments artifacts (manual export required today)

Operational play notes for SEs (what to do in the first 48 hours):
1) Triage questionnaire: mark each row as "info-only", "artifact-needed", or "decision-needed".
2) Attach standard artifacts for info-only.
3) Escalate decision-needed to product-security Slack and open JIRA-SEC ticket using template JIRA-SEC-NEW-Q (include scope and customer name).
4) If customer requires SIEM integration within 2 weeks, schedule a tech-call and reference GH-PR-2893 for the export connector.

Escalation contact list (fast):
- Product Security: marta.alvarez@redwood.com (primary), priya.desai@redwood.com
- Infra/Exports: evan.liu@redwood.com
- Legal/Privacy: daniel.kim@redwood.com

Open questions / TODOs (workshop items):
- Decide standard retention tiers to list in public one-pager (30/90/365) or provide customizable wording.
- Finalize canned redaction guidance for evidence automation (PII patterns).
- Confirm CEF field mapping for model_version and resource (GH issue).

Useful links (internal):
- RBAC v2 spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/RBAC-v2-spec
- Audit log schema canonical: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/Audit+ Schema+2025
- Evidence automation runner (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/evidence-runner/pull/2893
- Export connector RFC (JIRA): https://jira.redwood.com/browse/JIRA-SEC-514

Notes to self: keep this pocket guide < 2 pages when exported to PDF; make a one-slide executive-friendly summary. Meeting: align with Solutions on 2025-11-12 to validate standard snippets.

- 2025-11-05: updated artifact list and escalation flow (priyaa review)

End of doc.
